```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(knitr)
library(here)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(scales)
library(kableExtra)

opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)

stopifnot("Report knits inside the project" = file.exists(here("R", "utils.R")))



# HEADLINE NUMBERS ----

headline_files <- c(
  here("data", "processed", "phase2", c("national_headlines.csv", "case_study_daily_headlines.csv", "case_study_hourly_headlines.csv")),
  here("data", "processed", "phase3", "distribution_headlines.csv")
)

stopifnot("All four headline tables exist" = all(file.exists(headline_files)))

headlines <- headline_files %>%
  map(read_csv, col_types = cols_only(headline_id = col_character(), value = col_double(), unit = col_character())) %>%
  list_rbind()

stopifnot(
  "139 headline rows: 90 from Phase 2 and 49 from Phase 3" = nrow(headlines) == 139,
  "Headline IDs are unique" = !anyDuplicated(headlines$headline_id),
  "Every headline has a value" = !anyNA(headlines$value)
)

hl <- function(id) {
  value <- headlines$value[headlines$headline_id == id]
  stopifnot("Headline ID exists once" = length(value) == 1)
  value
}

hl_unit_count <- function(id) {
  unit <- headlines$unit[headlines$headline_id == id]
  stopifnot("Headline ID exists once" = length(unit) == 1)
  parse_number(unit)
}



# RECORDS FOR DATA AND METHODS ----

phase1_dir <- here("data", "processed", "phase1")
phase2_dir <- here("data", "processed", "phase2")

cleaning_log <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase1_dir, "cleaning_log.csv"),
  col_types = cols(step = col_character(), rows = col_double(), rows_removed = col_double())
)

hourly_cleaning_log <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase1_dir, "hourly_cleaning_log.csv"),
  col_types = cols(step = col_character(), rows = col_double(), rows_removed = col_double())
)

hourly_validation <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase1_dir, "hourly_validation.csv"),
  col_types = cols(check = col_character(), observed = col_character(), expected = col_character(), passed = col_logical())
)

weather_validation <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase1_dir, "weather_validation.csv"),
  col_types = cols(check = col_character(), observed = col_character(), expected = col_character(), passed = col_logical())
)

sites_by_year <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase2_dir, "national_sites_by_year.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(pollutant = col_character(), n_five_year_sites = col_double())
)

site_inventory <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase2_dir, "case_study_site_inventory.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(
    site_group = col_character(),
    local_site_name = col_character(),
    pollutant = col_character(),
    analysis_role = col_character(),
    km_to_channel = col_double(),
    method_change_date = col_date(),
    is_listed_method_change = col_logical()
  )
)

hourly_inventory <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase2_dir, "case_study_hourly_inventory.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(site_group = col_character(), local_site_name = col_character(), pollutant = col_character(), longest_wind_gap_days = col_double())
)

events <- read_csv(
  here("data", "reference", "events.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(event_name = col_character())
)

stopifnot(
  "Phase 1 hourly checks all passed" = all(hourly_validation$passed),
  "Phase 1 weather checks all passed" = all(weather_validation$passed),
  "Cleaning log starts at the raw import" = cleaning_log$step[1] == "Raw import",
  "Hourly log starts at the raw files" = hourly_cleaning_log$step[1] == "Raw hourly files",
  "16 hourly case-study monitors" = nrow(hourly_inventory) == 16
)

raw_daily_rows <- first(cleaning_log$rows)
clean_daily_rows <- last(cleaning_log$rows)
raw_hourly_rows <- first(hourly_cleaning_log$rows)
kept_hourly_rows <- last(hourly_cleaning_log$rows)

rebuilt_daily_maxima <- hourly_validation %>%
  filter(str_detect(check, "daily maximums rebuilt")) %>%
  pull(observed) %>%
  as.numeric() %>%
  sum()

weather_rows_read <- weather_validation %>%
  filter(str_detect(check, "^Rows read")) %>%
  pull(observed) %>%
  as.numeric()

five_year_sites <- sites_by_year %>%
  distinct()

harris_distances <- site_inventory %>%
  filter(!is.na(km_to_channel)) %>%
  distinct(local_site_name, km_to_channel)

last_site_inside <- harris_distances %>%
  filter(km_to_channel <= 7.5) %>%
  slice_max(km_to_channel, n = 1)

first_site_outside <- harris_distances %>%
  filter(km_to_channel > 7.5) %>%
  slice_min(km_to_channel, n = 1)

stopifnot(
  "Daily maxima rebuilt from three gases" = length(rebuilt_daily_maxima) == 1,
  "One weather row count" = length(weather_rows_read) == 1,
  "Five pollutants with five-year site counts" = nrow(five_year_sites) == 5,
  "One site on each side of the 7.5 km cutoff" = nrow(last_site_inside) == 1 && nrow(first_site_outside) == 1
)

daily_headlines <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase2_dir, "case_study_daily_headlines.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(headline_id = col_character(), value = col_double(), unit = col_character(), ci_low = col_double(), ci_high = col_double())
)

distance_gradients <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase2_dir, "case_study_distance_gradients.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(pollutant = col_character(), site_set = col_character(), n_sites = col_double(), rho = col_double(), p_value = col_double())
)

no2_leave_one_out <- distance_gradients %>%
  filter(pollutant == "NO2", str_detect(site_set, "without"))

weakest_leave_one_out <- no2_leave_one_out %>%
  slice_max(p_value, n = 1)

weakest_site_km <- site_inventory %>%
  filter(str_detect(weakest_leave_one_out$site_set, fixed(local_site_name)), !is.na(km_to_channel)) %>%
  distinct(km_to_channel) %>%
  pull(km_to_channel)

stopifnot(
  "30 daily headlines" = nrow(daily_headlines) == 30,
  "Ten NO2 leave-one-out runs" = nrow(no2_leave_one_out) == 10,
  "One weakest leave-one-out run" = nrow(weakest_leave_one_out) == 1,
  "One distance for the weakest run's dropped site" = length(weakest_site_km) == 1
)

no2_by_group <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase2_dir, "case_study_no2_by_group.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(site_set = col_character(), site_group = col_character(), year = col_double(), median_site_mean_ppb = col_double())
)

no2_site_years <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase2_dir, "case_study_no2_site_years.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(local_site_name = col_character(), year = col_double(), mean_daily_peak_ppb = col_double())
)

no2_method_changes <- site_inventory %>%
  filter(pollutant == "NO2", is_listed_method_change) %>%
  distinct(site_group, local_site_name, method_change_date)

park_place_change <- no2_method_changes$method_change_date[no2_method_changes$local_site_name == "Park Place"]
harvard_change <- no2_method_changes$method_change_date[no2_method_changes$local_site_name == "Houston Harvard Street"]

method_check_shifts <- no2_by_group %>%
  filter(site_set %in% c("Main", "Without days after method changes"), site_group != "Dallas-Fort Worth") %>%
  summarise(mean_ppb = mean(median_site_mean_ppb), .by = c(site_set, site_group)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = site_set, values_from = mean_ppb) %>%
  mutate(shift_ppb = `Without days after method changes` - Main)

ship_channel_shift <- method_check_shifts$shift_ppb[method_check_shifts$site_group == "Houston Ship Channel"]
houston_other_shift <- method_check_shifts$shift_ppb[method_check_shifts$site_group == "Houston other"]

park_place_before <- no2_site_years %>%
  filter(local_site_name == "Park Place", year <= 2022) %>%
  pull(mean_daily_peak_ppb) %>%
  mean()

park_place_after <- no2_site_years %>%
  filter(local_site_name == "Park Place", year >= 2024) %>%
  pull(mean_daily_peak_ppb) %>%
  mean()

month_year <- function(date) {
  str_c(month.name[as.integer(format(date, "%m"))], " ", format(date, "%Y"))
}

stopifnot(
  "Two listed NO2 method changes: Park Place and Harvard Street" =
    setequal(no2_method_changes$local_site_name, c("Park Place", "Houston Harvard Street")),
  "Park Place is a Ship Channel site" = no2_method_changes$site_group[no2_method_changes$local_site_name == "Park Place"] == "Houston Ship Channel",
  "One change date per site" = length(park_place_change) == 1 && length(harvard_change) == 1,
  "The group shifts rebuild the change in the Ship Channel lead" = abs((ship_channel_shift - houston_other_shift) - (hl("D06") - hl("D05"))) < 0.02,
  "The Ship Channel side gives most of the rise" = ship_channel_shift > 0.5 * (ship_channel_shift - houston_other_shift),
  "Park Place reads lower on its new method" = park_place_after < park_place_before
)

hourly_headlines <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase2_dir, "case_study_hourly_headlines.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(headline_id = col_character(), subject = col_character(), value = col_double(), ci_low = col_double(), ci_high = col_double())
)

ox_checks <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase2_dir, "case_study_ox_checks.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(
    site_set = col_character(), season = col_character(), ozone_gap_ppb = col_double(), no2_gap_ppb = col_double(),
    ox_gap_ppb = col_double(), ox_ci_low = col_double(), ox_ci_high = col_double(), share_of_ozone_gap_closed = col_double()
  )
)

ox_by_wind <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase2_dir, "case_study_ox_gap_by_wind.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(
    comparison = col_character(), site_set = col_character(), direction_type = col_character(), direction = col_character(),
    season = col_character(), ozone_gap_ppb = col_double(), no2_gap_ppb = col_double(), ox_gap_ppb = col_double(),
    ox_ci_low = col_double(), ox_ci_high = col_double(), share_of_ozone_gap_closed = col_double()
  )
)

calm_air <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase2_dir, "case_study_calm_air.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(site_set = col_character(), measure = col_character(), level = col_character(), calm_minus_windy_ppb = col_double(), ci_low = col_double(), ci_high = col_double())
)

so2_spike_sites <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase2_dir, "case_study_so2_spike_sites.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(site_set = col_character(), local_site_name = col_character(), pct_below_mdl = col_double(), spike_rate_per_1000 = col_double(), median_episode_hours = col_double())
)

seed_check <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase2_dir, "case_study_hourly_seed_check.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(finding_id = col_character(), verdict_changes = col_logical())
)

harvard_set <- "Without the transition band"

ox_year_checks <- ox_checks %>%
  filter(season == "All year")

calm_sites <- calm_air %>%
  filter(site_set == "Main", level == "Site")

main_so2_sites <- so2_spike_sites %>%
  filter(site_set == "Main")

stopifnot(
  "30 hourly headlines" = nrow(hourly_headlines) == 30,
  "Four Ox checks over the year" = nrow(ox_year_checks) == 4,
  "Harvard Street is the one transition-band check" = harvard_set %in% ox_checks$site_set,
  "Six calm-air sites for each measure" = all(count(calm_sites, measure)$n == 6),
  "Every calm-air NO2 and ozone range clears zero" =
    with(filter(calm_sites, measure != "Ox"), all(sign(ci_low) == sign(ci_high))),
  "Four SO2 spike sites" = nrow(main_so2_sites) == 4,
  "Every seed-check range has a verdict" = !anyNA(seed_check$verdict_changes)
)

hl_subject <- function(id) {
  subject <- hourly_headlines$subject[hourly_headlines$headline_id == id]
  stopifnot("Headline ID exists once" = length(subject) == 1)
  subject
}

distribution_headline_ranges <- read_csv(
  file.path(here("data", "processed", "phase3"), "distribution_headlines.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(headline_id = col_character(), ci_low = col_double(), ci_high = col_double())
)

headline_ranges <- bind_rows(
  select(daily_headlines, headline_id, ci_low, ci_high),
  select(hourly_headlines, headline_id, ci_low, ci_high),
  distribution_headline_ranges
)

hl_ci <- function(id, end) {
  row <- headline_ranges[headline_ranges$headline_id == id, ]
  stopifnot("Headline ID has one range" = nrow(row) == 1 && !is.na(row$ci_low), "End is low or high" = end %in% c("low", "high"))
  if (end == "low") row$ci_low else row$ci_high
}

ox_value <- function(set, season_name, column) {
  value <- ox_checks[[column]][ox_checks$site_set == set & ox_checks$season == season_name]
  stopifnot("One Ox check row" = length(value) == 1)
  value
}

so2_below_mdl_sites <- main_so2_sites %>%
  filter(pct_below_mdl > 90)

stopifnot(
  "Three SO2 sites mostly below the detection limit" = nrow(so2_below_mdl_sites) == 3,
  "One median spike length across sites" = n_distinct(main_so2_sites$median_episode_hours) == 1
)

five_year_n <- function(gas) {
  five_year_sites$n_five_year_sites[five_year_sites$pollutant == gas]
}

phase3_dir <- here("data", "processed", "phase3")

design_values <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase3_dir, "distribution_design_values.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(
    site_group = col_character(), local_site_name = col_character(), first_year = col_double(), design_value_ppm = col_double(),
    is_above_standard = col_logical(), gap_to_epa_ppm = col_double(), matches_epa = col_logical()
  )
)

design_value_years <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase3_dir, "distribution_design_value_years.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(local_site_name = col_character(), year = col_double(), completeness_pct = col_double(), fourth_ppm = col_double())
)

fit_checks <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase3_dir, "distribution_fit_checks.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(
    check = col_character(), version = col_character(), pollutant = col_character(), site_id = col_character(),
    comparison = col_character(), spread_gap = col_double(), gap_low = col_double(), gap_high = col_double()
  )
)

ozone_spread_gaps <- fit_checks %>%
  filter(check == "Group spread", pollutant == "Ozone")

t640_site_count <- fit_checks %>%
  filter(check == "Instrument", version == "T640 alone") %>%
  summarise(n = n_distinct(site_id)) %>%
  pull(n)

long_wind_gaps <- hourly_inventory %>%
  distinct(local_site_name, longest_wind_gap_days) %>%
  filter(longest_wind_gap_days > 100) %>%
  arrange(desc(longest_wind_gap_days))

near_zero_sites <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase3_dir, "distribution_site_inventory.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(pollutant = col_character(), site_id = col_character(), is_near_zero_site = col_logical())
) %>%
  filter(is_near_zero_site) %>%
  count(pollutant)

distribution_robustness <- read_csv(
  file.path(phase3_dir, "distribution_robustness.csv"),
  col_types = cols_only(finding_id = col_character(), result = col_character())
)

aldine_years <- design_value_years %>%
  filter(local_site_name == "Houston Aldine", year >= 2023) %>%
  arrange(year)

current_design_values <- design_values %>%
  filter(first_year == 2023)

design_value_misses <- design_values %>%
  filter(!matches_epa)

group_design_values <- current_design_values %>%
  summarise(median_ppm = median(design_value_ppm), .by = site_group)

spread_gap <- function(season, comparison_name) {
  row <- ozone_spread_gaps[ozone_spread_gaps$version == season & ozone_spread_gaps$comparison == comparison_name, ]
  stopifnot("One ozone spread gap row" = nrow(row) == 1)
  row
}

cool_spread_gaps <- ozone_spread_gaps %>%
  filter(version == "Cool season")

stopifnot(
  "Aldine has the three years of the 2023 to 2025 window" = identical(aldine_years$year, c(2023, 2024, 2025)),
  "22 case-study ozone sites per window" = nrow(current_design_values) == 22 && nrow(design_values) == 66,
  "Every miss against EPA is 0.001 ppm low" = all(abs(design_value_misses$gap_to_epa_ppm + 0.001) < 1e-9),
  "No miss changes a pass or fail, since every missed value is above the standard either way" = all(design_value_misses$design_value_ppm > 0.070),
  "PM2.5 sites with a T640 and enough days each side" = t640_site_count > 0,
  "Three case-study sites have a wind gap of over 100 days" = nrow(long_wind_gaps) == 3,
  "Three groups with a design value" = nrow(group_design_values) == 3,
  "The near-zero SO2 count matches its headline" = near_zero_sites$n[near_zero_sites$pollutant == "SO2"] == hl("F03"),
  "Three ozone spread comparisons in each season" = all(count(ozone_spread_gaps, version)$n == 3),
  "No cool-month ozone spread gap clears zero" = all(cool_spread_gaps$gap_low < 0 & cool_spread_gaps$gap_high > 0),
  "12 findings in the Phase 3 checks" = n_distinct(distribution_robustness$finding_id) == 12,
  "Every Phase 3 check holds or does not apply" = all(distribution_robustness$result %in% c("Holds", "Does not apply"))
)



# FORMATTING HELPERS ----

is_pdf <- is_latex_output()
ugm3 <- if (is_pdf) "µg/m$^3$" else "µg/m³"
chem <- function(formula, digit) {
  if (is_pdf) str_c(formula, "$_", digit, "$") else str_c(formula, "<sub>", digit, "</sub>")
}

table_format <- if (is_pdf) "latex" else "html"

report_side_figure <- function(path, record, width = 0.5, lines = NULL, label = NA_character_) {
  stopifnot("Figure file exists" = file.exists(path))
  has_label <- !is.na(label)
  if (has_label) {
    label_number <- str_extract(label, "^Figure [0-9A-Z.]+?\\.(?= )")
    stopifnot("A figure label starts with its number" = !is.na(label_number))
    label_finding <- str_remove(label, fixed(str_c(label_number, " ")))
  }
  if (is_pdf) {
    label_line <- if (has_label) {
      str_c("\\par\\vspace{-6pt}{\\sansfont\\scriptsize\\textbf{", label_number, "} ", label_finding, "}\n")
    } else {
      ""
    }
    asis_output(str_c(
      "\\begin{wrapfigure}", if (is.null(lines)) "" else str_c("[", lines, "]"), "{r}{", width, "\\linewidth}\n",
      "\\vspace{-14pt}\\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth]{", path, "}\n",
      label_line,
      "\\par\\vspace{-6pt}{\\sansfont\\scriptsize\\color{aqsgrey}Record: \\texttt{", str_replace_all(record, "_", "\\\\_"), "}}\n",
      "\\vspace{-10pt}\\end{wrapfigure}\n"
    ))
  } else {
    asis_output(str_c(
      "<figure class=\"report-figure side-figure\"><img src=\"", image_uri(path), "\" alt=\"", record, "\">",
      "<figcaption>", if (has_label) str_c("<strong>", label_number, "</strong> ", label_finding, "<br>") else "",
      "Record: <code>", record, "</code></figcaption></figure>"
    ))
  }
}

percent_sign <- if (is_pdf) "\\%" else "%"

rho_symbol <- if (is_pdf) "$\\rho$" else "ρ"

signed <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  str_replace(sprintf(str_c("%+.", digits, "f"), x), "^-", "−")
}
report_figure <- function(path, record, placement = "!tbp", label = NA_character_) {
  stopifnot("Figure file exists" = file.exists(path))
  has_label <- !is.na(label)
  if (has_label) {
    label_number <- str_extract(label, "^Figure [0-9A-Z.]+?\\.(?= )")
    stopifnot("A figure label starts with its number" = !is.na(label_number))
    label_finding <- str_remove(label, fixed(str_c(label_number, " ")))
  }
  if (is_pdf) {
    label_line <- if (has_label) {
      str_c(
        "\\par\\vspace{-4pt}{\\sansfont\\small\\textbf{", label_number, "} ",
        str_replace_all(label_finding, c("NO2" = "NO\\\\textsubscript{2}", "SO2" = "SO\\\\textsubscript{2}")), "}\n"
      )
    } else {
      ""
    }
    record_gap <- if (has_label && str_detect(label_finding, "NO2|SO2")) "-3pt" else "-6pt"
    latex <- str_c(
      "\\begin{figure}[", placement, "]\n",
      "\\makebox[\\linewidth][c]{\\includegraphics[width=1.103\\linewidth]{", path, "}}\n",
      label_line,
      "\\par\\vspace{", record_gap, "}{\\sansfont\\footnotesize\\color{aqsgrey}Record: \\texttt{", str_replace_all(record, "_", "\\\\_"), "}}\n",
      "\\end{figure}\n"
    )
    asis_output(latex)
  } else {
    label_html <- if (has_label) {
      str_c("<strong>", label_number, "</strong> ", str_replace_all(label_finding, c("NO2" = "NO<sub>2</sub>", "SO2" = "SO<sub>2</sub>")), "<br>")
    } else {
      ""
    }
    asis_output(str_c(
      "<figure class=\"report-figure\"><img src=\"", image_uri(path), "\" alt=\"", record, "\">",
      "<figcaption>", label_html, "Record: <code>", record, "</code></figcaption></figure>"
    ))
  }
}

style_table <- function(table, latex_options = "hold_position") {
  table %>%
    kable_styling(latex_options = latex_options, font_size = 9, full_width = FALSE) %>%
    row_spec(0, bold = TRUE)
}



# APPENDIX HELPERS ----

github_base <- "https://github.com/Yousef-sham5/houston-dfw-air-quality/blob/main/R/"

read_script <- function(file) {
  readLines(here("R", file), encoding = "UTF-8", warn = FALSE)
}

code_excerpt <- function(file, from, to, to_exact = FALSE) {
  lines <- read_script(file)
  start <- grep(from, lines, fixed = TRUE)[1]
  stopifnot("Excerpt start found" = !is.na(start))
  ends <- if (to_exact) which(lines == to) else grep(to, lines, fixed = TRUE)
  end <- ends[ends >= start][1]
  stopifnot("Excerpt end found" = !is.na(end))
  lines[start:end]
}

wrap_code_line <- function(line, width = 100) {
  if (nchar(line) <= width) return(line)
  chars <- str_split_1(line, "")
  in_string <- cumsum(chars == "\"") %% 2 == 1
  comma_ends <- which(chars == "," & !in_string & lead(chars) == " " & seq_along(chars) <= width)
  if (length(comma_ends) == 0) return(line)
  cut <- max(comma_ends)
  indent <- str_extract(line, "^ *")
  c(str_sub(line, 1, cut), wrap_code_line(str_c(indent, "    ", str_trim(str_sub(line, cut + 1), "left")), width))
}

code_block <- function(lines) {
  wrapped <- unlist(map(lines, wrap_code_line))
  stopifnot(
    "No code line is wider than the box" = all(nchar(wrapped) <= 110),
    "Wrapping keeps every character" = identical(str_remove_all(str_c(wrapped, collapse = ""), " "), str_remove_all(str_c(lines, collapse = ""), " "))
  )
  asis_output(str_c("```r\n", str_c(wrapped, collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n"))
}

script_link <- function(file) {
  if (is_pdf) {
    str_c("\\href{", github_base, file, "}{\\texttt{", str_replace_all(file, "_", "\\\\_"), "}}")
  } else {
    str_c("<a href=\"", github_base, file, "\"><code>", file, "</code></a>")
  }
}
```

# Introduction

The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) sets National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) for six criteria pollutants, with limits chosen to protect public health [1]. Many areas still do not meet them. In 2023, `r hl("N08")`% of ozone monitoring sites and `r sprintf("%.1f", hl("N09"))`% of annual PM2.5 sites with data in all five study years were above their standards (Section 3).

Houston and Dallas–Fort Worth both have long-running ozone problems. EPA classifies both metros as severe nonattainment areas for the 2008 ozone standard and serious nonattainment areas for the 2015 standard [2, 3]. In this dataset they rank `r hl("N16")`th and `r hl("N17")`th out of `r hl_unit_count("N16")` metros with an ozone exceedance, ranked by exceedance site-days. That count grows with the number of monitors a metro has, so it is only a rough comparison. The biggest difference between the two metros is the Houston Ship Channel. The channel and the area around it support what the American Society of Civil Engineers calls the second largest petrochemical complex in the world [4], with refineries, chemical plants and shipping concentrated along its banks.

The goal of this study is to measure how air near the Ship Channel compares with the rest of Harris County ("Houston other") and with Dallas–Fort Worth, and to check whether the differences match what the chemistry predicts. Three hypotheses are tested:

::: {.hypotheses data-latex=""}
**H1.** NO~2~ is higher near the channel. Combustion sources such as process heaters, flares, ship engines and diesel trucks all emit nitrogen oxides, so sites close to a dense cluster of them should read higher.

**H2.** Ozone is lower near the channel because fresh NO reacts with it: NO + O~3~ → NO~2~ + O~2~. Each ozone molecule used up makes one NO~2~ molecule, so the sum Ox = O~3~ + NO~2~ is conserved by this reaction. If titration explains the ozone gap, Ox should be about the same in both groups of sites.

**H3.** SO~2~ comes from short, local plumes. If so, it should show up as brief spikes that line up with certain wind directions, while the background stays near the detection limit.
:::

The analysis uses EPA Air Quality System (AQS) data from 2021 to 2025 at two scales. Daily data for PM2.5, ozone, NO~2~, SO~2~ and CO across the U.S. give the national picture. For the case study, hourly ozone, NO~2~ and SO~2~ from 16 monitors in Houston and Dallas–Fort Worth are paired with hourly wind and temperature. The Ship Channel group is defined as the `r hl("D01")` Harris County sites within 7.5 km of the channel's land-cut sections. The hourly groups are small, with two ozone and NO~2~ sites each, so the hourly results describe those specific sites. Each comparison is repeated with different site groupings and data subsets to check that it holds up. Because this is observational data, links to a source are stated as "consistent with" that source.

Section 2 covers the data and methods. Section 3 gives the national context, and Sections 4 and 5 present the daily and hourly case study. Section 6 describes how daily values are distributed, which curves fit them and how well those curves count high days, and works one ozone design value through EPA's rules to check it against EPA's published value. Section 7 lists the limitations, and Section 8 comes back to H1 to H3.



# Data and methods

## Data and cleaning

Data come from EPA's AirData pre-generated files [5], in the versions dated 25 June 2026: 25 daily, 15 hourly pollutant and 10 hourly weather files. Table 2.1 lists the parameter codes, daily values and standards. PM2.5 is limited to federal reference and equivalent methods (FRM and FEM), and the weather data are AQS wind speed, wind direction and temperature (61103, 61104, 62101).

```{r pollutant-table}
pollutant_table <- tribble(
  ~Pollutant,          ~`AQS code`, ~`Daily value`,         ~`Standard screened`,
  "PM2.5",             "88101",     "24-hour mean",         str_c("35 ", ugm3, ", 98th percentile day"),
  "PM2.5 (annual)",    "88101",     "Annual mean",          str_c("9.0 ", ugm3, ", mean of four quarters"),
  "Ozone",             "44201",     "Maximum 8-hour mean",  "0.070 ppm, 4th-highest day",
  chem("NO", 2),       "42602",     "Maximum 1-hour value", "100 ppb, 98th percentile day",
  chem("SO", 2),       "42401",     "Maximum 1-hour value", "75 ppb, 99th percentile day",
  "CO",                "42101",     "Maximum 8-hour mean",  "9 ppm, 2nd-highest day"
)

stopifnot("Six standards in the table" = nrow(pollutant_table) == 6)

pollutant_table %>%
  kable(
    format = table_format,
    caption = "Pollutants, AQS parameter codes, daily values and the NAAQS each site-year was screened against [1].",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    escape = FALSE,
    linesep = ""
  ) %>%
  column_spec(4, width = "2.5in") %>%
  style_table()
```

Cleaning took the daily files from `r comma(raw_daily_rows)` to `r comma(clean_daily_rows)` rows, mostly by removing duplicate summaries of the same monitor-day (Table A.1, Appendix). Gaps are never filled in, and daily values from days with under 75% of hours are dropped. Other unusual data, such as event days, hourly readings below the detection limit or on incomplete days, one monitor relocation and several method changes, are flagged and kept so each result can be rerun without them. Events are labelled from a sourced table of `r nrow(events)` state and county rows. The `r comma(raw_hourly_rows)` hourly rows were read in chunks down to `r comma(kept_hourly_rows)` monitor-hours for the 16 case-study monitors, and those hours rebuild all `r comma(rebuilt_daily_maxima)` daily maxima in EPA's daily files exactly. Times stay in local standard time, as AQS reports them.

## Site groups

The Ship Channel group is the Harris County sites within 7.5 km of the channel's 12 land-cut sections in the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers channel framework [6]. The cutoff falls between `r last_site_inside$local_site_name` (`r sprintf("%.2f", last_site_inside$km_to_channel)` km) and `r first_site_outside$local_site_name` (`r sprintf("%.2f", first_site_outside$km_to_channel)` km). The rest of Harris County is "Houston other", except Seabrook, which sits next to the separate Bayport industrial district. Dallas and Tarrant counties form Dallas–Fort Worth. Table 2.2 gives the sites in each group, and Section 4 maps the hourly sites.

```{r site-count-table}
group_order <- c("Houston Ship Channel", "Houston other", "Dallas-Fort Worth")
gas_order <- c("PM2.5", "Ozone", "NO2", "SO2")

daily_counts <- site_inventory %>%
  filter(analysis_role == "Main") %>%
  distinct(site_group, local_site_name, pollutant) %>%
  count(pollutant, site_group, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(scale = "Daily")

hourly_counts <- hourly_inventory %>%
  count(pollutant, site_group, name = "n") %>%
  mutate(scale = "Hourly")

site_counts <- bind_rows(daily_counts, hourly_counts) %>%
  mutate(site_group = factor(site_group, levels = group_order)) %>%
  arrange(scale, site_group) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(scale, site_group), values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(pollutant = factor(pollutant, levels = gas_order)) %>%
  arrange(pollutant)

stopifnot(
  "Four case-study pollutants" = nrow(site_counts) == 4,
  "Six count columns" = ncol(site_counts) == 7,
  "16 hourly monitors in the table" = sum(select(site_counts, starts_with("Hourly"))) == 16
)

site_counts %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("Hourly"), \(n) if_else(pollutant == "PM2.5", "–", as.character(n)))) %>%
  mutate(pollutant = recode(as.character(pollutant), NO2 = chem("NO", 2), SO2 = chem("SO", 2))) %>%
  kable(
    format = table_format,
    caption = "Sites per group. Daily counts are sites with data in all five years; hourly counts are the case-study monitors, which do not include PM2.5.",
    col.names = c("Pollutant", "Ship Channel", "Houston other", "DFW", "Ship Channel", "Houston other", "DFW"),
    booktabs = TRUE,
    escape = FALSE,
    align = c("l", rep("c", 6)),
    linesep = ""
  ) %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Daily, five-year sites" = 3, "Hourly monitors" = 3)) %>%
  style_table()
```

## How comparisons are tested

Groups are compared with same-day differences: each day, a group's value is the mean of its reporting sites, and subtracting two groups on the same day cancels most of the weather they share. The median daily difference gets a 95% range from a block bootstrap that resamples 14-day blocks 1,000 times, because neighbouring days are correlated. Each result is then rerun under up to eight checks, including alternative site groups such as the one in TCEQ's 2024 air toxics memo [7], added four-year sites, and dropping event days or the days after a monitor change. A check that leaves the data unchanged is dropped, and a result is said to hold when it keeps its sign with a range that excludes zero. Appendix A.3 shows the code for these steps.



# National context

## Network and screening

Levels use the sites with data in all five years (`r comma(five_year_n("Ozone"))` ozone, `r comma(five_year_n("PM2.5"))` PM2.5, `r five_year_n("NO2")` NO~2~, `r five_year_n("SO2")` SO~2~ and `r five_year_n("CO")` CO sites), and exceedance counts use all sites. Reporting SO~2~ and CO sites fell by `r abs(hl("N01"))`% and `r abs(hl("N02"))`%, and PM2.5 sites grew by `r hl("N03")`%. The FEM share of PM2.5 rose from `r hl("N04")`% to `r hl("N05")`%, with FEM reading `r hl("N06")` to `r hl("N07")` µg/m^3^ above FRM at the same site and day (Figure 2A.1, Appendix).

Each site-year was screened in its standard's own form, rounded as the regulations specify [8–12] (Figure 2A.2). Ozone and annual PM2.5 are missed most often: in 2023, `r hl("N08")`% of ozone sites and `r sprintf("%.1f", hl("N09"))`% of annual PM2.5 sites were above their levels, with the 9.0 µg/m^3^ annual PM2.5 level set in 2024 applied to every year. Over three-year windows, which are closer to EPA's design values, `r hl("N10")` to `r hl("N11")`% of ozone sites were above the standard.

```{r naaqs-figure}
report_figure(
  here("figures", "phase2", "2a.02_naaqs_near_standard.png"),
  "national_naaqs_screening.csv",
  placement = "H",
  label = "Figure 2A.2. Ozone and annual PM2.5 are missed most often."
)
```

## Events and metro ranks

Events matter much more for PM2.5 than for ozone (Figure 2A.4, Appendix). Labelled smoke, dust and storm days hold `r hl("N12")`% of PM2.5 exceedance site-days, and `r hl("N14")`% in 2023, the year of the large Canadian wildfire smoke episodes. Only `r hl("N15")`% of these event-day exceedances carry EPA's exceptional-event flag. For ozone the share is `r hl("N13")`%, consistent with ozone exceedances coming mainly from ordinary summer photochemistry. By exceedance site-days, Houston and Dallas–Fort Worth rank `r hl("N16")`th and `r hl("N17")`th of `r hl_unit_count("N16")` metros for ozone, against `r hl("N18")`nd and `r hl("N19")`th of `r hl_unit_count("N18")` for PM2.5 (Figure 2A.5, Appendix), so ozone is the main problem in both metros.

## Seasons and the weekend effect

Ozone peaks in June at `r hl("N21")` times its lowest month and PM2.5 in July at `r hl("N20")` times, consistent with summer photochemistry and, for PM2.5, wildfire smoke. NO~2~ and CO peak in winter at `r hl("N22")` and `r hl("N24")` times their lows, consistent with a shallow mixing layer that keeps fresh emissions near the ground. From April to October, weekend NO~2~ at the median site falls to `r sprintf("%.3f", hl("N26"))` of its weekday level while ozone stays at `r sprintf("%.3f", hl("N27"))`, because ozone does not follow NOx one for one. Where VOCs limit ozone formation, less NO on weekends means less titration, and ozone can rise. Weekend ozone is `r hl("N28")`% higher than on weekdays in Los Angeles, consistent with VOC-limited conditions, and `r abs(hl("N29"))`% and `r abs(hl("N30"))`% lower in Houston and Dallas–Fort Worth, consistent with more NOx-limited summer weekends (Figure 2A.10). Section 5 returns to titration at the hourly scale.

```{r weekend-figure}
report_figure(
  here("figures", "phase2", "2a.10_weekend_ozone.png"),
  "national_weekend_summary.csv, national_ozone_weekend_metros.csv",
  placement = "H",
  label = "Figure 2A.10. Weekend ozone rises in Los Angeles and falls in Houston and Dallas–Fort Worth."
)
```

# Houston case study: daily

```{r site-map}
report_side_figure(
  here("figures", "phase1", "case_study_sites_narrow.png"),
  "data/reference/case_study_sites.csv",
  width = round(3.2 / 6.5, 3),
  lines = 26,
  label = "Figure 1C.1. Nine case-study sites in three groups."
)
```

This section compares the three site groups using daily values at the sites with data in all five years (Table 2.2). Figure 1C.1 shows the hourly monitors used in Section 5. The daily groups include more Harris County sites, split by the same 7.5 km rule.

## NO~2~ and ozone by group

NO~2~ is highest at the Ship Channel in all `r hl("D04")` years. The median Ship Channel site's mean daily NO~2~ peak is `r hl("D05")` ppb above Houston other, or `r hl("D06")` ppb when the days after the NO~2~ method changes at Park Place (`r month_year(park_place_change)`) and Harvard Street (`r month_year(harvard_change)`) are left out, mostly because Park Place, a Ship Channel site, reads lower on its new method. NO~2~ also falls with distance from the channel. With four-year sites added, the Spearman correlation across `r distance_gradients$n_sites[distance_gradients$pollutant == "NO2" & distance_gradients$site_set == "With 4-year sites"]` sites is `r rho_symbol` = `r signed(hl("D07"))` (p = `r hl("D08")`). Dropping one site at a time keeps `r rho_symbol` between `r signed(min(no2_leave_one_out$rho))` and `r signed(max(no2_leave_one_out$rho))`, but without the farthest site (`r sprintf("%.1f", weakest_site_km)` km away), p rises to `r sprintf("%.3f", weakest_leave_one_out$p_value)`, so the gradient is treated as supporting evidence only.

Ozone shows the opposite pattern. Dallas–Fort Worth has the most ozone exceedance days per site in all `r hl("D02")` years, and the Ship Channel has the fewest in `r hl("D03")` of 5, consistent with fresh NO lowering ozone near the channel (H2).

## Same-day differences

Table 4.1 gives the same-day differences described in Section 2.3. The Ship Channel has `r hl("D19")` ppb more NO~2~ and `r abs(hl("D18"))` ppb less ozone than Houston other on the same days. More NO~2~ and less ozone on the same days is what titration predicts, and Section 5 tests this directly with Ox. Houston as a whole runs `r sprintf("%.2f", abs(hl("D22")))` ppb lower in ozone and `r hl("D23")` ppb higher in NO~2~ than Dallas–Fort Worth, holding in every run.

```{r paired-table}
paired_rows <- tribble(
  ~comparison,                        ~pollutant, ~result_id, ~runs_id, ~unit,
  "Ship Channel minus Houston other", "NO2",      "D19",      "D26",    "ppb",
  "Ship Channel minus Houston other", "Ozone",    "D18",      "D25",    "ppb",
  "Ship Channel minus Houston other", "PM2.5",    "D17",      "D24",    "ugm3",
  "Ship Channel minus Houston other", "SO2",      "D20",      "D27",    "ppb",
  "Houston minus Dallas–Fort Worth",  "NO2",      "D23",      "D30",    "ppb",
  "Houston minus Dallas–Fort Worth",  "Ozone",    "D22",      "D29",    "ppb",
  "Houston minus Dallas–Fort Worth",  "PM2.5",    "D21",      "D28",    "ugm3"
)

paired_table <- paired_rows %>%
  left_join(select(daily_headlines, result_id = headline_id, value, ci_low, ci_high), by = "result_id", relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  left_join(select(daily_headlines, runs_id = headline_id, runs_held = value, runs_unit = unit), by = "runs_id", relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  mutate(runs_total = parse_number(runs_unit)) %>%
  mutate(unit_label = if_else(unit == "ugm3", ugm3, "ppb")) %>%
  mutate(pollutant = recode(pollutant, NO2 = chem("NO", 2), SO2 = chem("SO", 2))) %>%
  transmute(
    Comparison = comparison,
    Pollutant = pollutant,
    `Median difference (95% range)` = str_c(signed(value), " (", signed(ci_low), " to ", signed(ci_high), ") ", unit_label),
    `Runs holding` = str_c(runs_held, " of ", runs_total)
  ) %>%
  mutate(Comparison = if_else(Comparison == lag(Comparison, default = ""), "", Comparison))

stopifnot(
  "Seven same-day results" = nrow(paired_table) == 7,
  "Every result has a range and a run count" = !anyNA(paired_table)
)

paired_table %>%
  kable(
    format = table_format,
    caption = str_c("Median same-day differences between groups, with block-bootstrap 95", if (is_pdf) "\\%" else "%", " ranges and the share of check runs in which each result holds its sign with a range clear of zero."),
    col.names = c("Comparison", "Pollutant", if (is_pdf) "Median difference (95\\% range)" else "Median difference (95% range)", "Runs holding"),
    booktabs = TRUE,
    escape = FALSE,
    align = c("l", "l", "l", "c"),
    linesep = c("", "", "", "\\addlinespace", "", "", "")
  ) %>%
  style_table()
```

PM2.5 and SO~2~ show no group gap worth reading. The PM2.5 difference holds in only `r hl("D24")` of `r hl_unit_count("D24")` runs, consistent with PM2.5 being mostly regional. The SO~2~ difference holds in every run, but at `r hl("D20")` ppb it sits far below the 2 ppb detection limit, so Section 5 reads SO~2~ through spike hours instead. Croquet, in Houston other, has more SO~2~ spike days than the average Ship Channel site in all `r hl("D11")` years. Figure 2B.7 in the Appendix shows these results by season, year and check.

## Events

Most Ship Channel monitors stopped reporting during Hurricane Beryl in July 2024. On average only `r hl("D12")`% of them reported during the event window, against `r hl("D13")`% in Houston other and `r hl("D14")`% in Dallas–Fort Worth (Figure 2B.6, Appendix). Winter Storm Uri raised PM2.5 to `r sprintf("%.2f", hl("D15"))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", hl("D16"))` times its normal level across the groups.

<!-- 2b: if space allows later, add one sentence on the ozone exceedance-day figure (2B.2) or the NO2-by-group figure (2B.3), both in the Appendix -->



# Houston case study: hourly

Hourly data show when the group gaps appear and how they depend on wind. Each group has two hourly ozone and NO~2~ sites, so these results describe those sites. Harvard Street is the one Houston other site 7.5 to 15 km from the channel, and because it changes the ozone result most, the main numbers are also given without it. All three groups report in the same hour in at least `r hl("H01")`% of hours.

## Daily cycles

Ship Channel NO~2~ is higher and its ozone lower than Houston other at all 24 hours, under every check. Both gaps are widest late in the day, with NO~2~ `r signed(hl("H02"), 1)` ppb at `r hl_subject("H02")` and ozone `r signed(hl("H03"))` ppb at `r hl_subject("H03")` (Figure 2C.2, Appendix). From April to October, 6 to 8 am NO~2~ on weekends is `r round(abs(hl("H04")))`% below weekdays at the Ship Channel, against `r round(abs(hl("H05")))`% in Houston other and `r round(abs(hl("H06")))`% in Dallas–Fort Worth. The smaller drop is consistent with more Ship Channel NO~2~ coming from sources that run all week, such as industry.

## The Ox balance

Titration (NO + O~3~ → NO~2~ + O~2~) turns each ozone molecule it destroys into one NO~2~ molecule, so it leaves Ox = O~3~ + NO~2~ unchanged. If titration were the only reason Ship Channel ozone is lower, the two groups would have the same Ox. Over the year, Ship Channel ozone is `r sprintf("%.2f", abs(hl("H07")))` ppb lower than Houston other (95% range `r sprintf("%.2f", abs(hl_ci("H07", "high")))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", abs(hl_ci("H07", "low")))`), but its Ox is only `r sprintf("%.2f", abs(ox_value("Main", "All year", "ox_gap_ppb")))` ppb lower, so **Ox closes `r round(hl("H08"))`% of the ozone gap** (Figure 2C.4, Table 5.1). Without Harvard Street it closes `r round(hl("H09"))`%, it closes at least `r floor(100 * min(ox_year_checks$share_of_ozone_gap_closed))`% under every check, and in winter, when little new ozone forms, the main Ox gap's range includes zero. This is consistent with fresh NO from channel sources using up ozone near where it is emitted. With no NO data, Ox cannot be split further into local and regional parts.

```{r ox-figure}
report_figure(
  here("figures", "phase2", "2c.04_ox.png"),
  "case_study_ox_checks.csv",
  placement = "H",
  label = "Figure 2C.4. Adding NO2 back closes at least half the ozone gap."
)
```

```{r ox-table}
ox_rows <- bind_rows(
  ox_checks %>%
    filter(site_set == "Main", season == "All year") %>%
    mutate(row = "All hours, all year"),
  ox_checks %>%
    filter(site_set == harvard_set, season == "All year") %>%
    mutate(row = "All hours, without Harvard Street"),
  ox_checks %>%
    filter(site_set == "Main", season == "Winter") %>%
    mutate(row = "All hours, winter"),
  ox_by_wind %>%
    filter(comparison == "Ship Channel minus Houston other", site_set == harvard_set, direction_type == "Channel or other", season == "All year") %>%
    mutate(row = if_else(direction == "From the channel", "Wind from the channel, without Harvard Street", "Other wind, without Harvard Street"))
)

stopifnot("Five Ox rows" = nrow(ox_rows) == 5)

ox_rows %>%
  mutate(ox_cell = if_else(
    is.na(ox_ci_low),
    signed(ox_gap_ppb),
    str_c(signed(ox_gap_ppb), " (", signed(ox_ci_low), " to ", signed(ox_ci_high), ")")
  )) %>%
  transmute(
    Hours = row,
    Ozone = signed(ozone_gap_ppb),
    NO2 = signed(no2_gap_ppb),
    Ox = ox_cell,
    `Gap closed` = str_c(round(100 * share_of_ozone_gap_closed), percent_sign)
  ) %>%
  kable(
    format = table_format,
    caption = "Ship Channel minus Houston other, ppb. Gap closed is the share of the ozone gap that Ox closes.",
    col.names = c("Hours", "Ozone", chem("NO", 2), "Ox", "Gap closed"),
    booktabs = TRUE,
    escape = FALSE,
    align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
    linesep = c("", "", "\\addlinespace", "", "")
  ) %>%
  style_table(latex_options = "HOLD_position")
```

## Calm air and wind

Calm hours, with wind below 0.5 m/s, make up `r sprintf("%.1f", hl("H14"))`% of hours at the Ship Channel, `r sprintf("%.1f", hl("H15"))`% in Houston other and `r sprintf("%.1f", hl("H16"))`% in Dallas–Fort Worth. Compared with windy hours at the same site, hour and month, calm hours carry `r sprintf("%.1f", min(filter(calm_sites, measure == "NO2")$calm_minus_windy_ppb))` to `r sprintf("%.1f", max(filter(calm_sites, measure == "NO2")$calm_minus_windy_ppb))` ppb more NO~2~ and `r sprintf("%.1f", abs(max(filter(calm_sites, measure == "Ozone")$calm_minus_windy_ppb)))` to `r sprintf("%.1f", abs(min(filter(calm_sites, measure == "Ozone")$calm_minus_windy_ppb)))` ppb less ozone at every site, each range clear of zero (Figure 2C.8, Appendix). In every group at least `r floor(hl("H19"))`% of the ozone lost in calm air shows up as NO~2~, consistent with titration in still air near the ground.

The Ox gap that titration leaves sits mostly in wind from the channel. Without Harvard Street, Ship Channel Ox is `r sprintf("%.2f", abs(hl("H28")))` ppb lower in wind from the channel but `r signed(hl("H29"))` ppb in other wind, a gap whose range includes zero (Table 5.1, Figure 2C.11 in the Appendix). This is consistent with ozone forming in channel air as it moves across Houston, so sites downwind of the channel gain Ox. NO~2~ also runs `r sprintf("%.1f", min(hl("H20"), hl("H21"), hl("H22"), hl("H23")))` to `r sprintf("%.1f", max(hl("H20"), hl("H21"), hl("H22"), hl("H23")))` times its usual level at all four Houston sites in wind from 60 to 90 degrees. A wind direction points toward a source without proving it, since each direction also brings its own kind of weather.

## SO~2~ plumes

SO~2~ is below the 2 ppb detection limit in `r sprintf("%.1f", min(so2_below_mdl_sites$pct_below_mdl))`% to `r sprintf("%.1f", max(so2_below_mdl_sites$pct_below_mdl))`% of hours at three of the four sites, so it is read through spike hours of 5 ppb or more. Spikes are short, with a median length of `r unique(main_so2_sites$median_episode_hours)` hour at every site. Croquet, in Houston other, spikes most often, at `r sprintf("%.1f", max(main_so2_sites$spike_rate_per_1000))` per 1,000 hours. Of its spikes, `r round(hl("H11"))`% fall between 9 am and 6 pm, and its summer rate is `r sprintf("%.1f", hl("H12"))` times any other season's, consistent with a raised plume mixed down to the ground by daytime heating. Most of its spike hours, `r round(hl("H24"))`%, come from the southwest, a direction that brings only `r round(hl("H26"))`% of its hours and points away from the channel (Figure 2C.10, Appendix). At Park Place, `r round(hl("H25"))`% of spike hours come from the channel side, which brings `r round(hl("H27"))`% of its hours. During Deer Park #2's spike hours, NO~2~ is `r sprintf("%.1f", hl("H13"))` ppb above normal (`r sprintf("%.1f", hl_ci("H13", "low"))` to `r sprintf("%.1f", hl_ci("H13", "high"))`), so the plumes carry nitrogen oxides as well. These patterns support H3: SO~2~ arrives in brief, local plumes from more than one direction.

## Robustness

All `r hl("H30")` headline hourly findings hold under every check that applies: without Harvard Street, without its hours after the method change, without Deer Park #2 after its move and without hours on the new wind sensors (Figure 2C.12, Appendix). All `r nrow(seed_check)` bootstrap ranges were redrawn with a second random seed, and `r if (sum(seed_check$verdict_changes) == 0) "none" else sum(seed_check$verdict_changes)` changed whether its range crosses zero.



# Distributions

Sections 3 to 5 compare average levels. Before these data go into any model, three more questions matter: what shape the daily values take, whether the groups differ in how much ozone swings from day to day, and whether a fitted curve counts high days correctly. At each five-year site, ordinary days are scaled by the site's mean and fitted with three common skewed curves (lognormal, gamma and Weibull), with a normal curve beside them for comparison. All three skewed curves have two parameters, so AIC, a standard score of fit, compares them fairly. Sites where a quarter or more of days sit at or below zero, almost all of them SO~2~ sites, are left out, which leaves `r comma(hl("F01"))` sites. A curve only counts as a clear winner if it keeps winning when the data are resampled in two-week blocks.

## Shape and fitted curves

Each site has to be read on its own. Pooling all sites together blurs the shape, because much of the spread then comes from differences between sites rather than from one day to the next. At almost every PM2.5 and SO~2~ site, and at most CO sites, the values are right-skewed: a few high days sit far above the rest, and a lognormal curve fits better than a normal one. Ozone is close to symmetric, and a normal curve fits better than a lognormal at `r round(hl("F10"))`% of ozone sites. NO~2~ falls in between, with no single shape winning clearly (Figure 3.5, Appendix).

These curve labels are less certain than they first look. Neighbouring days are linked, so five years of daily data hold less independent information than their size suggests. Once that is allowed for, the best curve for ozone stays the clear winner at only about half of the sites tested. For PM2.5 the monitor matters: the same sites lean much more strongly lognormal on a T640 monitor than on other monitors, consistent with an instrument effect whose cause is not confirmed. In practice, log-scale summaries suit PM2.5, SO~2~ and CO, ozone can be summarised on its normal scale, and PM2.5 comparisons across years should note when a site changed monitor.

## Ozone spread in the case study

Figure 3.6 compares how much ozone swings from day to day. The measure is a spread factor, which shows how many times above or below its usual level a site's ozone typically runs, so a larger factor means bigger swings. In warm months, Houston sites swing more than Dallas–Fort Worth sites, by `r sprintf("%.2f", min(hl("F23"), hl("F24")))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(hl("F23"), hl("F24")))` on this scale, and both ranges stay clear of zero. The Ship Channel and Houston other match each other, and in cool months no group differs. So the channel lowers ozone's level (Sections 4 and 5) without changing how much it swings. The warm-month gap covers all of Houston, consistent with the city switching between clean Gulf air and still, sunny days, though that cause is not tested here.

```{r spread-figure}
report_figure(
  here("figures", "phase3", "3.06_ozone_spread.png"),
  "distribution_fit_checks.csv",
  placement = "H",
  label = "Figure 3.6. Warm-month ozone swings wider at Houston sites."
)
```

## Counting high days

A curve can fit typical days well and still miss the rare high ones, which matters for any model that estimates how often a limit is passed. At most sites, the best-fitting curve misses the number of very high days, those above the site's 99th percentile, by more than 25%. Some of these misses cancel when sites are added together, yet for NO~2~ the curves still overcount high days by `r round(100 * (hl("F27") - 1))`% in total. The choice of curve matters as well. At the ozone standard, the best curves match the measured count, but a lognormal curve would predict about twice as many days above the limit as were actually measured.

For warm-month ozone in the case study, a gamma curve counts days above the standard well in all three groups, within the uncertainty of the measured count. It still overcounts the very highest days, the top 1% at each site, by `r round(100 * (min(hl("F38"), hl("F39"), hl("F40")) - 1))`% to `r round(100 * (max(hl("F38"), hl("F39"), hl("F40")) - 1))`%. Readings below the detection limit also matter. At Deer Park #2, treating them as "somewhere below the limit" instead of as exact values brings the predicted number of high SO~2~ days from about double the measured number down to about right. Fitted curves here describe the data. They should not stand in for counting the actual high days.

## A worked design value

An ozone design value is the three-year average of each year's 4th-highest daily 8-hour value, cut to three decimals. A site meets the standard at 0.070 ppm or below [11]. At Houston Aldine, the 4th-highest days were `r sprintf("%.3f", aldine_years$fourth_ppm[1])`, `r sprintf("%.3f", aldine_years$fourth_ppm[2])` and `r sprintf("%.3f", aldine_years$fourth_ppm[3])` ppm in 2023, 2024 and 2025. Their average, `r sprintf("%.4f", mean(aldine_years$fourth_ppm))`, is cut to `r sprintf("%.3f", hl("F43"))` ppm, the same value EPA publishes [13]. The site also just meets EPA's rule that at least 90% of days must be valid on average.

Repeating this for all 22 case-study ozone sites over three periods matches EPA at `r hl("F45")` of `r hl_unit_count("F45")` site-periods. The few misses are each 0.001 ppm low, because the daily cleaning drops short days that EPA keeps when they pass the limit, and none changes whether a site passes. All `r hl("F46")` sites are above the standard for 2023 to 2025, and the highest value is at Deer Park #2, a Ship Channel site. The three groups' typical design values are nearly the same, so the Ship Channel's lower average ozone does not carry over to its highest days. All `r hl("F49")` findings in this section hold under every check that applies (Figure 3.10, Appendix).



# Limitations

- **No trends.** Five years is too short to separate a trend from year-to-year weather, so changes between years are described but not tested.
- **Small groups.** Each group has two hourly ozone and NO~2~ sites, and Houston other has one five-year PM2.5 site, so the hourly results describe those sites rather than whole areas.
- **Pointers, not proof.** Distance to the channel's water stands in for distance to the plants along it, and each wind direction brings its own weather. Both point toward a source without proving it, which is why source claims say "consistent with".
- **No NO or NO~x~ data.** Ox shows how much of the ozone gap titration explains, but the rest cannot be split into local and regional parts.
- **Near the detection limit.** SO~2~ is below 2 ppb in most hours at three of the four sites, and the censored fits use method-wide detection limits, which can differ from a monitor's own.
- **Cleaning choices.** Days with under 75% of hours are dropped, which puts `r nrow(design_value_misses)` of `r nrow(design_values)` design values 0.001 ppm below EPA's, and Section 3's single-year screening is not a design value. Wind is missing for up to `r long_wind_gaps$longest_wind_gap_days[1]`, `r long_wind_gaps$longest_wind_gap_days[2]` and `r long_wind_gaps$longest_wind_gap_days[3]` days in a row at `r str_remove(long_wind_gaps$local_site_name[1], "^Houston ")`, `r str_remove(long_wind_gaps$local_site_name[2], "^Houston ")` and `r str_remove(long_wind_gaps$local_site_name[3], "^Houston ")`.
- **Monitor changes.** PM2.5 moved toward FEM monitors, and Park Place and Harvard Street changed their NO~2~ methods in `r month_year(park_place_change)` and `r month_year(harvard_change)`. Checks drop the affected days, but comparisons between years still partly reflect the monitor mix.
- **Many comparisons.** Dozens of ranges are reported without a multiple-comparison adjustment, so the results that hold under every check are the safest to cite.
- **Curves describe, they do not forecast.** Tail checks test fit on the measured days only.



# Conclusion and regulatory implications

**H1 is supported.** Ship Channel NO~2~ is higher than Houston other in all `r hl("D04")` years, on the same days (`r signed(hl("D19"))` ppb, range `r signed(hl_ci("D19", "low"))` to `r signed(hl_ci("D19", "high"))`) and at all 24 hours, under every check. The distance gradient agrees but rests partly on one far site.

**H2 is supported in part.** Ship Channel ozone is lower on the same days (`r signed(hl("D18"))` ppb, range `r signed(hl_ci("D18", "low"))` to `r signed(hl_ci("D18", "high"))`) and at every hour. Adding NO~2~ back closes `r round(hl("H08"))`% of the hourly ozone gap, or `r round(hl("H09"))`% without Harvard Street, so titration explains at least half of it. The Ox gap that remains sits in wind from the channel, consistent with ozone forming in channel air as it moves downwind.

**H3 is supported.** SO~2~ arrives as spikes with a median length of `r unique(main_so2_sites$median_episode_hours)` hour over a background below the detection limit, from the southwest at Croquet (`r round(hl("H24"))`% of its spike hours) and from the channel side at Park Place (`r round(hl("H25"))`%), consistent with more than one local source.

These results carry three implications for air quality planning, each limited by the observational design.

**Lower ozone near the channel is not cleaner air.** Much of the ozone missing near the channel shows up as NO~2~, and the Ox left over is consistent with ozone forming downwind. Every case-study ozone site, Ship Channel sites included, is above the 0.070 ppm standard for 2023 to 2025, and the highest design value is at Deer Park #2. This is consistent with treating NO~x~ near the channel and ozone across Houston as one problem.

**SO~2~ is best read hourly, at more than one site.** One-hour spikes from different directions disappear in daily means and can be missed by a single monitor, which matters for the 1-hour SO~2~ standard.

**Method choices move the answer.** Monitor changes, site groupings and the choice of curve each shift results enough to matter: a default lognormal roughly doubles ozone exceedance counts, and the share of the ozone gap that Ox closes depends on whether Harvard Street is included. Analyses that feed decisions should state these choices and rerun the main result under each one, as this report does.

Run `R/0_setup.R` once, then the scripts in the order of Table A.2.   filter(step != "Raw import") %>%

```{r code-map}
code_map %>%
  mutate(file = map_chr(file, script_link)) %>%
  mutate(n_lines = comma(n_lines)) %>%
  kable(
    format = table_format,
    caption = "Scripts in run order, with links to the source on GitHub.",
    col.names = c("Script", "What it does", "Main outputs", "Lines"),
    booktabs = TRUE,
    escape = FALSE,
    align = c("l", "l", "l", "r"),
    linesep = ""
  ) %>%
  column_spec(2, width = "2.4in") %>%
  column_spec(3, width = "1.75in") %>%
  style_table()
```

## A.3 Key code {-}

These excerpts are read from the scripts each time the report is built, so they always match the code behind the results.

**NAAQS screening** (`utils.R`). Each site-year gets its standard's statistic (a ranked daily value, or the mean of four quarterly means for annual PM2.5), rounded the way the standard specifies, and is compared with the level.

```{r excerpt-naaqs}
code_block(code_excerpt("utils.R", "naaqs_statistics <- function(", "}", to_exact = TRUE))
```

**Chunked hourly read** (`utils.R`). Each 1-million-row chunk is filtered to the case-study monitors before the next is read, so the full hourly files never sit in memory, and the result is cached until the zip changes.

```{r excerpt-chunks}
code_block(c(code_excerpt("utils.R", "keep_case_study_rows <- function(", "}", to_exact = TRUE), "", code_excerpt("utils.R", "filter_case_study_zip <- function(", "}", to_exact = TRUE)))
```

**Same-day differences and the block bootstrap** (`2b_daily_case_study.R`). The median daily difference gets a 95% range from resampled 14-day blocks, which keeps the correlation between neighbouring days.

```{r excerpt-bootstrap}
code_block(c(code_excerpt("2b_daily_case_study.R", "block_bootstrap_range <- function(", "}", to_exact = TRUE), "", code_excerpt("2b_daily_case_study.R", "summarise_differences <- function(", "}", to_exact = TRUE)))
```

**Dropping checks that change nothing** (`2b_daily_case_study.R`). A check whose days and values match the main run exactly would only add resampling noise, so it is removed before any range is drawn.

```{r excerpt-drop}
code_block(code_excerpt("2b_daily_case_study.R", "difference_series <- daily_differences %>%", "anti_join(unchanged_checks"))
```

**The Ox balance** (`2c_hourly_eda.R`). Ozone, NO~2~ and Ox gaps are taken in the same hour, and the share of the ozone gap that Ox closes is one minus the Ox gap over the ozone gap.

```{r excerpt-ox}
code_block(c(code_excerpt("2c_hourly_eda.R", "ox_paired_gaps <- ox_long %>%", "mutate(gap_ppb = ship_channel_ppb - houston_other_ppb)"), "", code_excerpt("2c_hourly_eda.R", "ox_checks <- ox_season_gaps %>%", "arrange(season, site_set)")))
```
